title: CORS origin check allows all origins when SCOUT_EXTENSION_ID is not configured
explanation: When `SCOUT_EXTENSION_ID` is not set, `origin` is `null` and the CORS middleware is configured with `origin: false`. However, the manual origin check on line 221 only blocks requests whose `Origin` header is present AND does not match `origin`. When `origin` is `null`, any request with an `Origin` header passes the check (`req.get('origin') !== null` is true, but `null !== null` is false, so the condition `req.get('origin') !== origin` evaluates to `true` only when origin is a string). Wait — re-reading: if `origin` is `null` and a request sends `Origin: http://evil.example`, then `req.get('origin')` is truthy and `req.get('origin') !== origin` is `'http://evil.example' !== null` which is `true`, so the request IS blocked. The actual gap is that when `extensionId` is set but the extension sends no `Origin` header (e.g. from a non-browser context), the check passes. The more concrete issue is that the server binds only to 127.0.0.1, which limits exposure, but the origin check logic is subtle and worth auditing.
observation: The origin guard returns 403 only when `req.get('origin')` is truthy AND differs from the configured `origin`. Requests without an `Origin` header always pass regardless of the configured extension ID.
required_conditions: A caller that can reach 127.0.0.1:3456 sends a POST without an Origin header
SCOUT_EXTENSION_ID is configured, meaning the server expects only the extension to call it
fix_hint: When `extensionId` is configured, require the `Origin` header to be present and equal to the expected chrome-extension URL. Add a check: `if (origin && !req.get('origin')) return res.status(403).json({error: 'origin_required'});`
